title: DLMF 1.16 Distributions: Let \phi be a function defined on an open interval I=(a,b) , which can be infinite.
summary: DLMF 1.16 Distributions: Let \phi be a function defined on an open interval I=(a,b) , which can be infinite.
body: NIST DLMF section 1.16 (Distributions) says: "Let \phi be a function defined on an open interval I=(a,b) , which can be infinite. The closure of the set of points where \phi\not=0 is called the support of \phi . If the support of \phi is a compact set (§ 1.9(vii) ), then \phi is called a function of compact support . A test function is an infinitely differentiable function of compact support. A sequence \{\phi_{n}\} of test functions converges to a test function \phi if the support of every \phi_{n} is contained in a fixed compact set K and as n\to\infty the sequence \{\phi_{n}^{(k)}\} converges uniformly on K to \phi^{(k)} for k=0,1,2,\dots . The linear space of all test functions with the above definition of convergence is called a test function space . We denote it by \mathcal{D}(I) . A mapping \Lambda:\mathcal{D}(I)\rightarrow\mathbb{C} is a linear functional if where \alpha_{1} and \alpha_{2} are real or complex constants. \Lambda:\mathcal{D}(I)\rightarrow\mathbb{C} is called a distribution , or generalized function , if it is a continuous linear functional on \mathcal{D}(I) , that is, it is a linear functional and for…" Equation 1.16.1 on the page has alt text "\Lambda(\alpha_{1}\phi_{1}+\alpha_{2}\phi_{2})=\alpha_{1}\Lambda(\phi_{1})+% \alpha_{2}\Lambda(\phi_{2}),". Equation 1.16.2 on the page has alt text "\lim_{n\to\infty}\Lambda(\phi_{n})=\Lambda(\phi).". This card records that section's wording and equation alt text. It does not retypeset a formula the alt text did not carry.
